findings.issue: The frontier-admit.cjs role row lists the CLI commands as seed, admit, close, block and graph. It leaves out the new `budget` command. runCli accepts six commands (frontier-admit.cjs:1110-1112), and `budget` routes to writeSeedBudget (frontier-admit.cjs:1118), which rewrites maxIterations in the config. Both workflows' step_frontier_budget calls it.

evidence.cmd: rg -n "expected seed, admit, close, graph, block or budget|command === 'budget'" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs
evidence.out:
1112: throw new Error(`unknown command: ...; expected seed, admit, close, graph, block or budget`);
1118: if (command === 'budget') return writeSeedBudget({ artifactDir, target });

fix.new: Owns the node store and the seed, admit, close, block, graph and budget calls the flag turns on.

findings.issue: The deep-research.yaml row says it owns step_frontier_seed and step_frontier_admit. The workflow also owns step_frontier_budget (deep-research.yaml:775), which runs `frontier-admit.cjs budget` (deep-research.yaml:788) to size a defaulted expansive budget from the seed.

The deep-review.yaml row says it owns step_frontier_seed and step_frontier_admit. The workflow also owns step_frontier_budget (deep-review.yaml:930), which runs `frontier-admit.cjs budget --target review` (deep-review.yaml:943).

The admission paragraph says what relevance includes ('a node's scope sitting inside a file-list review target'). It does not say that relevance now also prunes a proposal whose question, or any scope entry, is over 500 characters. Control characters are first replaced with spaces. An operator who sees a `relevance` prune on an in-target proposal gets no hint that length is the cause. Code: MAX_PROPOSAL_TEXT_LENGTH = 500 (frontier-admit.cjs:54), the isOverLength checks inside relevance (frontier-admit.cjs:583-584) and cleanProposalText (frontier-admit.cjs:140-147).

The doc says an expansive run 'adds two more' state files, frontier-nodes.jsonl and frontier-seed.json, and the table (lines 47-48) lists only those two. step_frontier_admit also writes {artifact_dir}/frontier-known-texts.json before every admission and passes it as --known-texts (deep-review.yaml:2019-2026). No step deletes it, so an expansive run leaves a third file, the per-iteration dedupe input.

evidence.out:
2020:          JSON array of strings to {artifact_dir}/frontier-known-texts.json holding every
2026:        command: '... frontier-admit.cjs admit --target review ... --known-texts "{artifact_dir}/frontier-known-texts.json"'
